@caesarxuchao - the problem happens with Binding as well. And any subresource which can be created as mentioned here: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/80426#discussion_r306928468

We can fix the fake Bind() in the same way.

For other subresources, there is no fake method implemented for them, so we don't need to worry about them.

I agree that creating a pod object perhaps is not right.

I think we need to investigate what users expect to see.

For the real Evict method, apiserver is in the background is going to check if the podDisruptionBudget is satisfied and if so, it deletes the pod (see [code](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/registry/core/pod/storage/eviction.go)). This is too complicated. I don't think we will ever implement this behavior in the fake. 

Then the question is, after calling the fake Evict, and then call a fake List for the pods, what do users expect to see? Do they want to see the pod gone? I think we need to ask the issue reporter what their exact use case is.

The case is simpler for Bind. For the Bind, the real implementation is [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/32f6ca5b67f9f1eb3124488e8ef3d8214a857ab2/pkg/registry/core/pod/storage/storage.go#L159-L183). It sets the pod.spec.host. In the fake, we can update the pod as well. But do users actually need this complex behavior? I think in most use cases, user just wants to validate that their client isssues a call to Bind(), and the current implementation satisfies that need.

@caesarxuchao - you're right about users just wanting to verify the Evict or Bind is called. The original issue reported was that pods could not be listed after Evict or Bind is called. Bouke, along with raising the issue raised a PR: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/80426. The PR shows that the fake is used only to verify if evict or Bind is called and not actually change the pod spec or delete the pod. Based on the issue reporter's intention, can't we just update Evict() and Bind() to return the subresource obj and not actually invoke the Create action?
@caesarxuchao - any updates?

Thanks for confirming the use case.

I think we still need to call fake.Invoke(), because we need to trigger this [line](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/77bedd891d822a68f65a77df792ed9dbd7ceaad6/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/testing/fake.go#L135) to record the action. Users usually checks the recorded actions to verify if an action was triggered as expected.

There are a few ways to fix this:
1. Prepend custom reactors when creating the fake clientset [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/77bedd891d822a68f65a77df792ed9dbd7ceaad6/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/kubernetes/fake/clientset_generated.go#L130). The custom reactor would only handle verb=create, and resource=pod/evict. The custom reactor will return "handled", so it short-circuits the `testing.ObjectReaction(o)`.  I don't know if this approach will cause any backwards-incompatible behavior, maybe some users expect there to be only one default reactor.

2. Expanding the [tracker](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/77bedd891d822a68f65a77df792ed9dbd7ceaad6/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/testing/fixture.go#L197), to allow adding custom handler that handles special cases like Evict(). Note that we would still want to keep fixture.go generic. The custom handler should be injected when the fake clientset is [created](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/77bedd891d822a68f65a77df792ed9dbd7ceaad6/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/kubernetes/fake/clientset_generated.go#L120).

3. This is expedient . We still call fake.Invoke, but leaving `action.Object` empty, then it will trigger this [error condition](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/77bedd891d822a68f65a77df792ed9dbd7ceaad6/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/testing/fixture.go#L390), and then we ignore this error, i.e.,

```golang
 func (c *FakePods) Evict(ctx context.Context, eviction *policy.Eviction) error {
     action := core.CreateActionImpl{}
     action.Verb = "create"
     action.Namespace = c.ns
     action.Resource = podsResource
     action.Subresource = "eviction"
     action.Object = nil

     c.Fake.Invokes(action, eviction)
     return nil
 }
```
